REGULAR MEETING AGENDA
CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS
AND THE SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY
THURSDAY - MARCH 11, 2021 - 07:00 P.M.
ZOOM VIDEO COMMUNICATIONS, MEETING ID # 892 1303 4633
LEGISLATIVE BODY MEMBERS MAY PARTICIPATE FROM THE CITY COUNCIL CHAMBER, 18125 BLOOMFIELD AVENUE, OR VIA TELECONFERENCE AUTHORIZED BY STATE OF CALIFORNIA EXECUTIVE ORDERS N-25-20 AND N-29-20
* THE CITY COUNCIL CHAMBER REMAINS CLOSED TO THE PUBLIC *
INSTRUCTIONS FOR PUBLIC PARTICIPATION IN THIS MEETING ARE LISTED BELOW
*COVID-19 NOTICE*
To protect public health and safety during the local, state, and federally declared COVID-19 emergency, and in compliance with the current Los Angeles County Health Officer Order, the City Council Chamber remains closed to the public. As authorized by State of California Executive Orders N-25-20 and N-29-20 this meeting will be conducted via teleconference. Public observation and participation in this meeting will be facilitated through the methods described below.
Agenda Materials
The complete agenda for this meeting is available on-demand at www.cerritos.us and at the Office of the City Clerk, 18125 Bloomfield Avenue, 1st floor, Cerritos, CA, during regular business hours (Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., weekend and observed holidays excepted). Any materials submitted to the legislative body after the distribution of this agenda will be available for public inspection in the Office of the City Clerk during regular business hours. Requests for agenda materials or meeting participation assistance can also be made by email to city_clerk@cerritos.us or by phone at (562) 916-1248 during regular business hours.
PUBLIC OBSERVATION AND PARTICIPATION
The public can observe the meeting via livestream on the City’s website at www.cerritos.us, on cable television at Cerritos TV3, or by connecting to the ZOOM meeting described below.
Public Comments
Members of the public may provide public comment for this meeting using any of the following methods:
Written correspondence (hard copy or email): Public comments can be submitted via email to city_clerk@cerritos.us or by hard copy to the Office the City Clerk no later than 3:00 p.m. on the day of the meeting. Please identify the agenda item number in the subject line of the email or hard copy document. All written correspondence received by the 3:00 p.m. deadline will be distributed to the legislative body prior to the meeting. During the meeting, your name and summary comments will be read into the record. The document will be retained with the public record of the meeting.
Teleconference Participation: Live audio public comments can be made by connecting to the meeting using the information listed below. Public speakers will be queued to provide comment at the appropriate time during the meeting agenda and must be available at the time they are called upon to speak.
Cerritos Zoom meeting online link: https://us02web.zoom.us/j/89213034633
Cerritos Zoom Meeting call-in telephone number: (669) 900-6833
Cerritos Zoom Meeting ID: 892 1303 4633
Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) Accommodations
In compliance with the ADA, any person with a disability who requires accommodation in order to participate in a meeting should contact the Office of the City Clerk at (562) 916-1248 to request accommodation. The City will use its best efforts to provide reasonable accommodations related to the teleconference meeting.

MINUTES OF A REGULAR MEETING OF THE CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL AND THE
SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY HELD MARCH 11,
2021, 7:00 P.M., IN HYBRID MODE FROM THE COUNCIL CHAMBER, 18125
BLOOMFIELD AVENUE, CERRITOS, CA AND VIA TELECONFERENCE AS AUTHORIZED BY
STATE OF CALIFORNIA EXECUTIVE ORDERS N-25-20 AND N-29-20, VIA ZOOM VIDEO
COMMUNICATIONS, MEETING ID# 892 1303 4633

1.  Call to Order

  The meeting was called to order at 7:00 p.m.

2.  Invocation

  The invocation was given by Vida Barone, City Clerk/Treasurer.

3.  Pledge of Allegiance

  The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Mayor Naresh Solanki.

4.  Roll Call

  The following members of the City Council/Successor Agency were in attendance:

  Council/Agency Member Bruce Barrows
  Council/Agency Member Grace Hu
  Council/Agency Member Frank A. Yokoyama
  Mayor Pro Tem/Vice Chair Chuong Vo
  Mayor/Chair Naresh Solanki

5.  Presentations/Appointments

  Proclamations were made by the City Council as follows:

  Merrell Eugene Williams (in honor of his 100th birthday celebration on March 11, 2021).

  Women’s History Month (March 2021).

  American Red Cross Month (March 2021).

  Mayor Solanki spoke regarding the Cerritos Sculpture Garden Memorial Illumination in honor
  of Cerritos residents who had succumbed to COVID-19. Photographs of the Memorial
  Illumination were displayed in the official meeting PowerPoint presentation.

  CLOSED SESSION REPORT

  Pam Lee, Interim City Attorney, provided the following report from the Tuesday, March
  9, 2021, 2:00 p.m. City Council/Successor Agency Special Meeting Closed Session:

  The City Council met in Closed Session to discuss Item 5A as listed on the Tuesday,
  March 9, 2021, 2:00 p.m. agenda:

  5A.  PUBLIC EMPLOYMENT
  Pursuant to California Government Code Section 54957(b) (COUNCIL)
  Title: City Attorney

  With regard to Item 5A, the City Council discussed the matter and no reportable action
  was taken. This concluded the Closed Session report from the Tuesday, March 9, 2021,
  2:00 p.m. City Council/Successor Agency Special Meeting.
 City of Cerritos  March 11, 2021, 7:00 p.m.
City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting  Page 2 of 6

6.  Public Comments and Suggestions

  The Mayor opened the public comments period.

  Written correspondence:
  (Written correspondence is considered public record and full-text copies of submitted
  written correspondence can be obtained in the Office of the City Clerk/Treasurer)

  Edward Stanila submitted written correspondence regarding creating a City policy to ban
  gas powered leaf blowers.

  Audio public comments:

  Edward Stanila spoke in support of creating a City policy to ban gas powered leaf
  blowers.

  Gabrielle Babcock, representing the Soroptimist International Artesia-Cerritos Club,
  thanked the City Council for their support of Women’s History Month.

  Daisy Legasca spoke regarding caring for senior citizens during the COVID-10 pandemic
  and inquired whether the City Council information on the City’s website was accurate.

  Noting there were no other individuals who provided written correspondence or elected
  to speak, the Mayor declared the public comments period closed.

7.  Consent Calendar

7A.  Approval of Minutes

  Approval of the February 25, 2021, 7:00 p.m., City Council/Successor Agency Regular
  Meeting Minutes (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  MOTION: It was moved by Barrows, and seconded by Vo, to approve the February 25,
  2021, 7:00 p.m., City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting Minutes
  (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Barrows, Hu, Yokoyama, Vo, Solanki
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

  Approval of the March 1, 2021, 2:00 p.m., City Council Special Meeting Minutes
  (COUNCIL).

  MOTION: It was moved by Barrows, and seconded by Vo, to approve the March 1, 2021,
  2:00 p.m., City Council Special Meeting Minutes, as amended in the revised agenda
  report (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Barrows, Hu, Yokoyama, Vo, Solanki
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None
 City of Cerritos  March 11, 2021, 7:00 p.m.
City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting  Page 3 of 6

7.  Consent Calendar (continued)

7B.  Approval of the Register of Demands

7B.1. Approval of the Register of Demands for the City of Cerritos dated March 11, 2021
  (COUNCIL).

  MOTION: It was moved by Barrows, and seconded by Vo, to approve the Register of
  Demands as follows:

  City of Cerritos  03/11/2021  $ 2,039,889.69 (COUNCIL)

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Barrows, Hu, Yokoyama, Vo, Solanki
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

7B.2. Approval of the Register of Demands for the Successor Agency to the Cerritos
  Redevelopment Agency dated March 11, 2021 (SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  MOTION: It was moved by Barrows, and seconded by Vo, to approve the Register of
  Demands as follows:

  Successor Agency  03/11/2021  $ 3037.00 (SUCCESSOR AGENCY)

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Barrows, Hu, Yokoyama, Vo, Solanki
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

7C.  Approval of Treasurer's Reports

  Approval of the City Council/Successor Agency Treasurer's Reports for the period ending
  January 31, 2021 (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  MOTION: It was moved by Barrows, and seconded by Vo, to approve the City
  Council/Successor Agency Treasurer’s Reports for the period ending January 31, 2021
  (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Barrows, Hu, Yokoyama, Vo, Solanki
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

8.  Public Hearings

  None.
 City of Cerritos  March 11, 2021, 7:00 p.m.
City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting  Page 4 of 6

9.  New and Old Business

9A.  Review and consideration of an informational update on the City's response to the
  COVID-19 local emergency (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Annie Hylton, City Librarian & Marketing Manager. A
  PowerPoint presentation was displayed.

  The Mayor opened the public comments period. Noting there were no individuals who
  provided written correspondence or elected to speak, the Mayor declared the public
  comments period closed.

  MOTION: It was moved by Vo, and seconded by Hu, to receive and file the
  informational report on the City's response to the COVID-19 local emergency
  (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Barrows, Hu, Yokoyama, Vo, Solanki
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

9B.  Review and consideration to waive full reading of and adopt A RESOLUTION OF THE
  CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS IN SUPPORT OF THE LOS ANGELES COUNTY
  METROPOLITAN TRANSPORTATION AUTHORITY’S COMPLETE STREETS POLICY
  (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was presented by Ana Tenorio, Management Analyst. A PowerPoint
  presentation was displayed.

  The Mayor opened the public comments period. Noting there were no individuals who
  provided written correspondence or elected to speak, the Mayor declared the public
  comments period closed.

  MOTION: It was moved by Barrows, and seconded by Hu, to defer consideration of this
  item to a future meeting to allow staff to conduct research related to the impact of
  adopting the subject resolution on the City’s position on the West Santa Ana Branch Line
  project (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (4 - 1) as follows:

  AYES:  Barrows, Hu, Vo, Solanki
  NOES:  Yokoyama
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

9C.  Review and consideration of the program for the temporary installation of sculptures in
  the Cerritos Sculpture Garden – generally located in the Cerritos Civic Center on the
  northwest corner of Bloomfield Avenue and 183rd Street, west of the Cerritos Sheriff’s
  Station (APN 7028-028-904) (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Kathy Matsumoto, Assistant City Manager. A PowerPoint
  presentation was displayed.
 City of Cerritos  March 11, 2021, 7:00 p.m.
City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting  Page 5 of 6

9.  New and Old Business (continued)

9C.  (continued)

  The Mayor opened the public comments period. Noting there were no individuals who
  provided written correspondence or elected to speak, the Mayor declared the public
  comments period closed.

  MOTION: It was moved by Vo, and seconded by Barrows, to:

  1. Authorize compensation from the Art in Public Places Trust Fund for the temporary
  installation of sculptures in the Cerritos Sculpture Garden for the two-year period
  from February 2019 through February 2021, as follows:

  Artist  Art Piece  Compensation (Feb. 2019 – Feb. 2021)

  Jeff Zischke  “Joker”  $2,500 ($1,250/year)
  Lyle London  “Artemis”  $2,500 ($1,250/year)

  ; and

  2. Refer the following items to the Fine Arts and Historical Commission for their review
  and consideration:

  a. Temporary art piece installation program (including recommendations on art
  pieces which will be forwarded to the City Council for their final approval); and

  b. Negotiation with the respective artists of the final purchase price for the “Joker”
  and “Artemis” art pieces and forwarding recommendations to the City Council for
  their final approval (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Barrows, Hu, Yokoyama, Vo, Solanki
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

10.  Legislative Items

10A.  Report on pending legislation.

  None.

10B.  Review and consideration to support or oppose specific legislation in the State or
  Federal legislature or in the State or Federal Executive Office for signature.

  None.

11.  City Council Communications/Committee Reports/Report on Meetings

  A report was provided by Councilmember Barrows.

  Pam Lee, Interim City Attorney, stated the funds collected in the Art in Public Places
  Trust Fund are restricted by law and can be utilized only for the purpose for which they
  were collected.
 City of Cerritos  March 11, 2021, 7:00 p.m.
City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting  Page 6 of 6

11.  City Council Communications/Committee Reports/Report on Meetings
  (continued)

  CONSENSUS (Barrows): Directed the City Clerk to remove Item 201 from the
  Consensus List as use of the funds collected in the Art in Public Places Trust Fund are
  restricted by law and are to be utilized only for the purpose for which they were
  collected.

12.  Closed Session

  Pam Lee, Interim City Attorney, announced the City Council would recess to Closed
  Session to discuss the item listed on the Closed Session agenda. An announcement
  regarding any reportable action resulting from the Closed Session will be made at the
  next regular meeting.

12A.  CONFERENCE WITH LEGAL COUNSEL – ANTICIPATED LITIGATION
  Pursuant to California Government Code Section 54956.9(d)(4) (COUNCIL)
  Number of cases: One (1)

13.  Adjournment

  The meeting adjourned at 9:05 p.m.

  /s/Vida Barone
  Vida Barone, City Clerk/Agency Secretary
ATTEST:

/s/Naresh Solanki
Naresh Solanki, Mayor/Chair
